**8. PROGRAMME AND PROGRESS REPORTING**

8.1 Master Programme

The Master Programme, Revision F, dated 12 March, was accepted by the Project Manager on 19 March. It defines the key dates and sequence of operations for the works. The Contractor shall maintain and update the Master Programme monthly, or more frequently if required, to reflect actual progress and any approved variations.

8.2 Progress Meetings

Progress meetings shall be held fortnightly at the site office. The Contractor shall issue an agenda at least two working days prior to each meeting. Minutes shall be issued within five working days of the meeting. The following standing items shall be included on the agenda:

(a) health, safety, and environmental matters;
(b) progress against the Master Programme;
(c) quality control and testing;
(d) variations and change control;
(e) payment applications;
(f) any matters raised by the Project Manager or the Supervisor.

8.3 Monthly Progress Report

The Contractor shall submit a monthly progress report to the Project Manager no later than five working days after the end of the reporting period. The report shall include:

(a) a summary of work completed during the period;
(b) a comparison of actual progress against the Master Programme, including any slippage and proposed recovery measures;
(c) details of any work not in accordance with the Works Information and any corrective actions;
(d) records of labour, plant, and materials on site;
(e) results of all tests and inspections carried out during the period;
(f) a list of any accidents or incidents, with details of any investigations;
(g) a summary of any variations instructed and quotations submitted;
(h) a current risk register update;
(i) any matters that may affect the completion date or the quality of the works.

8.4 Interim Payment Applications

Interim payment applications shall be submitted monthly, no later than the 25th day of each month. Each application shall be accompanied by a detailed breakdown of the work completed, the value of materials on site, and any deductions or adjustments. The Project Manager shall certify payment within fourteen days of receipt of the application. The Contractor shall provide such supporting information as the Project Manager may reasonably require to verify the application.

The Contractor shall maintain records of all inspections and tests, including the results, and shall provide copies to the Supervisor upon request. Any defective work shall be identified, marked, and corrected at the Contractor’s expense.

Any work that does not conform to the Works Information shall be recorded on a Non-Conformance Report (NCR). The Contractor shall investigate the cause of the non-conformance, propose corrective actions, and submit the NCR to the Supervisor for approval. Corrective actions shall be implemented promptly, and the work shall be re-inspected.
